title: Investigating health-promoting effects of fiber-rich food and their fermentability by the gut microbiota
summary: Dietary fiber is fermented by gut bacteria to metabolites that exert various health-promoting effects in the intestine, particularly short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). Under typical Western dietary conditions, the abundance of specific gut bacteria is often reduced, so that an increased fiber intake does not necessarily lead to higher levels of health-promoting SCFAs. Our previous studies have shown that many populations in Sub-Saharan Africa follow traditional diets that are naturally rich in specific types of dietary fibers, namely resistant starch. Their gut microbiota also contains high numbers of SCFA-producing bacteria. In this project, we investigate the relationship between increased intake of resistant starch and health-promoting effects, such as enhanced SCFA production. We conduct a short dietary intervention with healthy volunteers, comparing two forms of resistant starch delivery: Western-style food product enriched with resistant starch and a traditional East African dish that is naturally high in resistant starch. We hypothesize that, despite identical daily resistant starch intake, the food matrix influences the microbial fermentation of resistant starch into SCFAs. Overall, we expect that resistant starch supplementation will increase SCFA concentrations in the participants’ gut.
conditions: Investigation of the health-promoting effects of dietary fiber-rich foods and their fermentation by the gut microbiota.

interventions.name: For the next five days, study participants will receive daily cookies fortified with resistant starch. Participants will undergo anthropometric measurements, complete a food frequency questionnaire, and provide a stool sample both before and after the five-day intervention.

Study participants will consume a traditional East African plantain dish (Matooke), high in resistant starch, for five consecutive days. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Caucasian
Exclusion criteria:
• Not living in Germany within the last 5 years
• Pregnancy/breastfeeding
• Chronic diseases of the digestive system (inflammatory bowel diseases, colorectal cancer, diverticulitis)
• Antibiotic use within the last 4 weeks
• Regular use of probiotics (discontinued at least 2 weeks before intervention)
• Acute diseases of the digestive system (diarrhea)
• Family history of chronic bowel-related diseases
